section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what minimum age can a Kansas resident apply for a learner's permit?
note: Kansas has the lowest minimum permit age in the United States — 14 years old. This is a highly tested Kansas-specific fact. Most other states require applicants to be 15 or 16. Kansas permits 14-year-olds to begin learning to drive under adult supervision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Kansas allows teenagers to apply for a restricted license at age 15 after holding a permit since age 14. What is this arrangement called?
options: a:Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL),b:Early Operator Program,c:Provisional Teen License,d:Junior Operator Permit
note: Kansas uses a Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) system. A teen gets a learner's permit at 14, a restricted license at 15 (after meeting supervised driving requirements), and a full unrestricted license at 16. The GDL system progressively reduces restrictions as experience builds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in Kansas when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: Kansas sets the default urban speed limit at 30 mph when no other limit is posted. This is consistent with many neighboring Midwestern states. Always look for posted signs, as specific business or school areas may have different limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Kansas highways when no sign is posted?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: The default highway speed limit in Kansas is 65 mph when no sign is posted. Interstate highways typically have a higher posted limit of 75 mph. The 65 mph default applies to most two-lane and four-lane non-interstate highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on most Kansas interstate highways?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Kansas interstates have a maximum speed limit of 75 mph for passenger vehicles. This is higher than many states. Always check posted signs, and remember that urban interstate sections through cities like Wichita or Kansas City may have lower limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in Kansas school zones?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: Kansas school zones have a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or warning lights are active. This is lower than many states' 25 mph school zone limits. Reduce speed well in advance of school zones and watch carefully for children near the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Kansas's zero tolerance law, what BAC level is illegal for a driver under 21?
options: a:Any measurable amount — 0.00%,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: Kansas sets the illegal BAC threshold for drivers under 21 at 0.02%. A driver under 21 with a BAC at or above 0.02% faces DUI charges and license suspension. The standard adult DUI limit is 0.08% for drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in Kansas?
note: Kansas sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. A BAC at or above 0.08% is sufficient to establish impairment under Kansas law. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Kansas's GDL program, teens under 16 with a restricted license cannot drive during which hours?
options: a:8 PM to 5 AM,b:9 PM to 5 AM,c:10 PM to 6 AM,d:Midnight to 5 AM
note: Kansas restricts drivers under 16 from driving between 9 PM and 5 AM. This curfew ensures new teenage drivers avoid nighttime driving — the highest-risk period — until they have more experience. Exceptions apply for work, school activities, and emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Kansas's implied consent law means that by driving in Kansas, you have agreed to:
options: a:Allow your vehicle to be searched at any time,b:Submit to a chemical test if suspected of DUI,c:Always wear a seatbelt,d:Pay all traffic fines without contest
note: Kansas's implied consent law means that operating a vehicle on Kansas roads constitutes automatic consent to chemical testing if a law enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to suspect DUI. Refusing a test results in license suspension and the refusal may be used as evidence in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus ahead displays flashing red lights and an extended stop arm on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop only if you are directly behind the bus,b:Slow to 20 mph and proceed carefully,c:Stop at least 20 feet from the bus — in both directions — until lights stop flashing,d:Yield only if children are visible stepping off the bus
note: On a two-lane undivided road in Kansas, vehicles traveling in BOTH directions must stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. Do not move until the arm retracts and lights stop flashing. On a divided highway with a physical median, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Kansas's Move Over law require when you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Move over only for police and fire vehicles,b:Stop completely until the vehicle moves,c:Move one lane away if safe, or slow to a reasonable speed if lane change is not possible,d:Maintain speed but activate hazard flashers
note: Kansas's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, towing, or utility vehicle with flashing lights. If moving over is not safely possible, reduce to a safe and appropriate speed for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The recommended following distance under normal driving conditions in Kansas is:
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Kansas recommends the 3-second following distance as the minimum under normal conditions. Pick a fixed landmark — when the car ahead passes it, you should not reach it for at least 3 seconds. In poor weather or at highway speeds, increase to 4–6 seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are at a 4-way stop and two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time — one directly across from you, and one to your right. Both of you are going straight. Who goes first?
options: a:You go first since you are going straight,b:The vehicle to your right goes first,c:The vehicle directly across goes first since it faces you,d:Whoever accelerates first proceeds
note: When two vehicles arrive at a 4-way stop simultaneously, the driver to your RIGHT has the right of way. In this scenario, even though the vehicle directly across arrives at the same time, the vehicle to your right takes priority because of the yield-to-right rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning right on a red light in Kansas is:
options: a:Prohibited statewide,b:Permitted after a complete stop, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Permitted without stopping if no traffic is visible,d:Only allowed between 7 AM and 9 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Kansas after a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic. Some busy intersections display 'No Turn on Red' signs — always check. Never proceed without first coming to a full stop and verifying the path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light in Kansas means:
options: a:Yield to cross traffic, then proceed when clear,b:Slow and proceed with caution without stopping,c:Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe,d:The signal is malfunctioning — use your own judgment
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look in all directions, yield to existing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clearly safe. A flashing yellow means caution — slow down but stopping is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Kansas two-lane road, which of the following indicates a no-passing zone?
options: a:A broken white line on the right edge of the road,b:A broken yellow center line on your side,c:A solid yellow line on your side of the center,d:A double white line at the edge of the road
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line prohibits passing. You must not cross the center to overtake another vehicle. A broken yellow line on your side indicates that passing is permitted when safe and clear. Always check both sides of the center stripe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Kansas, all vehicle occupants are required to:
options: a:Wear a seatbelt only if the vehicle is moving over 30 mph,b:Wear a seatbelt — all occupants in all seating positions,c:Wear a seatbelt only in the front seat,d:Wear a seatbelt only on highways
note: Kansas requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear seats — to wear a properly adjusted seatbelt. Kansas has primary enforcement, meaning an officer can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation without needing another reason.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from behind in Kansas, you must:
options: a:Speed up and turn at the next intersection,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until the vehicle passes,d:Move to the left lane to give the emergency vehicle the right lane
note: Kansas law requires you to pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from any direction. Do not move until the vehicle has completely passed. Never block an intersection while pulling over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Kansas road and see a yellow diamond-shaped sign with a curved arrow. This indicates:
options: a:A mandatory turn is coming up,b:A curve or winding road ahead — adjust speed,c:You are approaching a yield sign,d:A traffic signal is ahead
note: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a curved arrow warns of a curve or winding road ahead. Reduce speed to safely navigate the curve. Warning signs like this are not regulatory (you are not required to turn) — but ignoring the warning is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a pedestrian crosswalk and a pedestrian is waiting at the curb. Kansas law requires you to:
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and continue through the crosswalk,b:Honk to signal your presence, then proceed,c:Stop and yield the entire roadway until the pedestrian has completely crossed,d:Stop only if the pedestrian is already in the crosswalk
note: Kansas law requires drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians at crosswalks — including those waiting at the curb who have not yet stepped into the road. You must yield the entire roadway, not just your lane. Failing to yield to pedestrians is a moving violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on most Kansas interstates through major cities?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Kansas interstates through major urban areas like Wichita and Kansas City typically have a posted limit of 65 mph — lower than the rural interstate limit of 75 mph. Always follow the posted sign. Urban sections are often congested and require extra vigilance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Kansas highway, you see a school bus ahead with AMBER (yellow) flashing lights. This means:
options: a:The bus is moving — maintain your speed,b:The bus is about to stop — slow down and prepare to stop,c:The bus has already stopped — come to a complete stop now,d:Passing the bus on the left is permitted
note: Amber (yellow) flashing lights are the school bus's advance warning that it is preparing to stop. Slow down and be ready to stop completely. When lights switch to flashing red and the stop arm extends, you must stop. Amber lights give you the precious seconds needed to reduce speed safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in most Kansas residential neighborhoods when no sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: The default speed limit in Kansas residential areas is 25 mph when no speed limit sign is posted. This lower speed limit in neighborhoods gives drivers more time to react to children playing, pets, cyclists, and pedestrians who may enter the roadway unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Kansas, a teen aged 15 driving alone with a restricted license must be off the road by what time at night?
options: a:8 PM,b:9 PM,c:10 PM,d:Midnight
note: Kansas drivers under 16 with a restricted license must not drive between 9 PM and 5 AM. This nighttime curfew applies to 15-year-olds driving independently on a restricted license. Exceptions exist for work, school activities, and emergencies with a parent's permission.

question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, what happens to your level of impairment?
options: a:You become more intoxicated.,b:You become more coordinated.,c:You become more sober.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream. As BAC goes up, your judgment, reaction time, coordination, and ability to drive safely all get worse. Higher BAC always means more impairment, not less.

question: What are common consequences of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It cannot result in a traffic citation.,b:It can frustrate others and may result in a citation.,c:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.
note: Tailgating (following too closely) increases the risk of rear-end collisions and often angers or frightens other drivers. It is considered unsafe driving and can lead to traffic citations for following too closely or aggressive driving.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the proper immediate response?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and brake lightly as you slow down.,b:Apply the brake hard to stop immediately.,c:Pull over sharply without slowing gradually first.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and stay straight in your lane. Do not slam on the brakes; instead, ease off the accelerator, let the car slow gradually, and then brake lightly as needed. Once under control and at a safe speed, steer off the road to a safe place.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the right (toward the edge of the road).,b:Keep them straight ahead.,c:Turn them toward the center of the road (left).
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic without reason, what will likely happen?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic flow and possibly receive a citation.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You demonstrate proper defensive driving technique.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic for no valid reason can block or disrupt the normal flow of vehicles. This can be unsafe and may result in a citation for impeding traffic. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic, within the posted speed limit and as conditions allow.

question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which direction should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Toward the right, toward the side of the road.,c:Toward the left, toward the center of the road.
note: On a downhill slope with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the right, toward the edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Both directions may pass.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross it only to turn left when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries, you should move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is drivable and safe to do so. This helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic flowing.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: On an interstate, if you must stop, pull completely onto the shoulder, turn on your hazard flashers, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened if it is safe. Walking along the interstate is very dangerous.

question: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane and is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield if at a corner.
note: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or a white cane, you must always yield the right-of-way. Stop well before the crosswalk and allow them to cross safely, and never honk or try to direct them verbally.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is correct?
options: a:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,b:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,c:Medications are safe to take at any time if prescribed by a doctor.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, especially cold and allergy medications, can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Even when taken as directed, they can impair driving. Always read labels and talk with your doctor or pharmacist about how a medication may affect your ability to drive.

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.
note: When you are coming out of a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk. Only after the sidewalk is clear and it is safe may you continue into the street and then yield to traffic on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before slowing or stopping, check your mirrors and be aware of traffic behind and beside you. This helps you brake smoothly, signal in time, and avoid being hit from the rear by a driver who is not paying attention.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does that indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the proper immediate action?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly to slow the car.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Once the vehicle slows and you have it under control, steer smoothly to the side of the road and brake gently to a stop in a safe place.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway even when there is no marked crosswalk.

question: What is the only thing that will lower a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Drinking caffeine.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed up the reduction of blood alcohol concentration; they may make you feel more awake but you are still impaired.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, how must you respond?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling over to the right side of the road and stopping. Stay stopped until the vehicle has passed, unless a police officer or other official directs you otherwise.

question: Which factors commonly contribute to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions greatly increases your risk of a crash. Higher speeds reduce your time to react and increase stopping distance and crash severity.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Maintain your normal speed.
note: Work zones often have lane shifts, workers close to traffic, and unexpected stops. You should slow down, obey all work zone signs and flaggers, and be ready to stop suddenly for equipment, workers, or other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Beep your horn.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Before moving back into your original lane after passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space and will not cut the other driver off when you return to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after coming to a full stop?
options: a:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,b:Whenever you yield to other traffic at the intersection.,c:Only when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
note: In many U.S. states, you may turn left on red only when you are on a one‑way street turning onto another one‑way street, after coming to a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and only if there is no sign prohibiting the turn.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra room to turn and may swing wide, creating a squeeze zone between the vehicle and the curb. You should wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its right turn before you turn, so you are not trapped or struck in their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when is the correct time to start slowing?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Stay at highway speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane. Once in the deceleration lane, begin slowing to the posted ramp or exit speed. Slowing too early in the through lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be traveling?
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic speed.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of freeway traffic, as long as it is safe and within the speed limit. Entering much slower than the flow makes merging difficult and can cause other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: When is it inappropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or to alert others to your presence when necessary. Near blind pedestrians, rely on yielding, slowing, and giving them extra space. A sudden horn blast can be confusing or frightening for someone using sound cues to navigate, and may actually reduce their safety.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to compete with them.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, do not engage, challenge, or try to compete. Stay calm, create space, and safely let them pass or move away from you. Avoid eye contact and gestures; your goal is to reduce the chance of a confrontation or crash.

question: How does excessive speed typically affect driver behavior?
options: a:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,b:It often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:It does not increase the chance of a crash.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and often leads to risky choices such as tailgating, unsafe passing, and late braking. Excessive speed greatly increases both the chance of a crash and the severity of any collision.

question: When is the most hazardous time for turning or stopping on a rainy day?
options: a:One half hour after rain stops.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: The first 20–30 minutes of rain are usually the most dangerous. Water mixes with oil and other residues on the road surface, making it especially slippery. After steady rain for a longer period, much of this residue is washed away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back on immediately.,b:Turn the front wheels sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently if needed to slow down. Do not jerk the steering wheel back onto the road; instead, after you have slowed and checked for traffic, steer smoothly back onto the pavement.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what size gap should you look for?
options: a:Four- to five-second gap in traffic.,b:Two- to three-second gap in traffic.,c:Three- to four-second gap in traffic.
note: Before changing lanes, you should look for a gap large enough to let you move over without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve. A four‑ to five‑second gap gives you time to signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and complete the lane change smoothly while keeping a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead in your new lane.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass when which condition is met?
options: a:The vehicle ahead moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The yellow line next to your side is broken.,c:The opposite side's yellow line is broken.
note: Double yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may only cross them to pass when the line closest to your lane is broken and you have enough clear distance to pass safely. If the line next to you is solid, you must not cross it to pass, even if the other side’s line is broken.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and be prepared to yield if necessary. Unlike a steady red or flashing red, a flashing yellow does not require you to stop if the way is clear.

question: To check your vehicle's blind spots, what should you do?
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder into the blind spot.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas just to the side and slightly behind your car are blind spots. To check these areas before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move while still keeping control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed and proceed through carefully.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

question: At a red traffic light that also displays a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Be in the appropriate lane and the intersection is clear.,c:Wait until the main light turns green.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in that direction. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow when you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have your lights on, which should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beams.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, you should use your low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off fog, rain, or snow and make it harder to see, and parking lights alone are not sufficient for seeing or being seen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful when attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: Passing is prohibited in marked no‑passing zones and at or on railroad crossings because sight distance and safety are limited. Both actions are illegal and create a high risk of collision with oncoming traffic or trains.

question: What increased risk does fatigue while driving present?
options: a:Being late for an appointment.,b:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Driver fatigue slows reaction time, harms judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Nodding off, even for a moment, can lead to a serious crash because you may leave your lane or fail to react to hazards.

question: If the rear of your car begins to skid left, what should you do?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer to the left (in the direction you want the car to go).,c:Steer to the right.
note: In a skid, you should ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. If the rear of your car skids left, you steer left to help straighten the vehicle and regain control, avoiding sudden braking or jerky steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's instructions?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only if children are present.
note: You must always obey a school crossing guard’s instructions whenever they are directing traffic, regardless of the time of day or whether you see children present. Crossing guards have legal authority similar to traffic control devices, and ignoring them is both unsafe and illegal.

question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.,b:Signal only and change lanes quickly.,c:Only check your mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you should signal to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and then check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. This sequence helps ensure the lane is clear and reduces the risk of sideswipe collisions.

question: When a large truck ahead is turning right on a multi-lane street, what might it do?
options: a:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,b:May complete the turn in either lane.,c:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
note: Large trucks often need to swing wide to the left before making a right turn because their rear wheels follow a tighter path than the front wheels. You should never try to squeeze between a turning truck and the curb, and give the truck extra space to complete the turn safely.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
note: You should check your rearview mirrors frequently to stay aware of traffic behind you, including vehicles that may be following too closely or preparing to pass. Regular mirror checks help you anticipate hazards and make safer decisions when slowing, stopping, or changing lanes.

question: In inclement weather, what is the recommended steering and braking technique?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In rain, snow, ice, or other poor conditions, you should steer and brake smoothly to avoid skids. Abrupt steering or hard braking can cause your tires to lose traction. Gentle, gradual inputs help you maintain control and give your tires the best chance to grip the road.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a vehicle that cannot see behind it (trucks, buses, vans, trailers).,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: You should leave extra following distance behind large vehicles like trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers because their size creates large blind spots and blocks your view of the road ahead. More space gives you extra time to react if they stop suddenly or if hazards appear in front of them.

question: What is the nature of having a driver's license?
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: In the United States, driving is considered a privilege, not a right. The state grants you a license if you meet certain requirements, and that license can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it legal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings permit passing.,b:Within the curve where you see no oncoming vehicles.,c:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.
note: You may only pass where signs and pavement markings indicate that passing is allowed, such as a broken center line with no “No Passing” signs. Passing is unsafe and generally illegal in intersections and on curves or hills where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When they are clean and dry.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Roads are usually most slippery just after it starts to rain. Oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the first water and create a slick film. After it has been raining for a while, much of this buildup is washed away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: How does driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic usually affect safety?
options: a:It is often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and attempt risky passes.,b:It is a good idea if the weather is bad.,c:It is appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake, change lanes, or attempt risky passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of surrounding traffic when it is safe and within the posted speed limit, adjusting for conditions like weather or visibility.

question: If your vehicle is equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) and you need to stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Gradually press the brake pedal.,b:Pump the brake pedal repeatedly.,c:Firmly press the brake pedal and hold it.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and keep steady pressure on it. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control, so you should not pump the brakes yourself.

question: If a school bus ahead of you in your lane has its red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed after you think all children have left the bus.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm (if equipped) is withdrawn. This applies in both directions unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median between you and the bus.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when on a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the right curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the left curb.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn should be made from the lane closest to the left curb, because that lane is already aligned with the direction of the turn and minimizes conflicts with other traffic.

question: What is the first driving-related ability alcohol affects?
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making, even before obvious physical skills like balance or clear vision. Poor judgment leads to risky choices such as speeding, following too closely, or misjudging gaps in traffic, which greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian who began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' started flashing is still in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait until the pedestrian has crossed before proceeding.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian in the intersection; wait until they have cleared the roadway before moving.

question: If your car's suspension is failing, what problem can result?
options: a:Slack in the steering.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Vehicle control problems.
note: A failing suspension can cause the vehicle to bounce excessively, lean or sway in turns, and respond poorly to steering input. This makes it harder to keep the car stable and in your lane, especially during sudden maneuvers, so loss of vehicle control is the main safety concern.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are collisions more likely to occur?
options: a:When one vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,b:When all vehicles travel at the same speed.,c:When one lane travels faster than the others.
note: Crashes are more likely when one vehicle is moving significantly faster or slower than surrounding traffic. Large speed differences increase lane changes, tailgating, and sudden braking, which all raise collision risk. Traveling at a speed that reasonably matches the flow (while staying within the speed limit) is generally safer.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: When oncoming headlights blind you at night, you should avoid looking directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the lane line or road edge as a guide until the vehicle passes. This reduces glare and helps you maintain proper lane position.

question: What is the main purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:To warn inattentive drivers by creating vibration and sound when a vehicle leaves the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are designed to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle in the lane.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should move it as far off the main-traveled portion of the road as possible, ideally with all four wheels completely off the roadway. This reduces the chance of being struck by passing traffic and improves safety for you and other road users.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Traffic light ahead.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you are in a no‑passing zone. You must not cross this line to pass another vehicle, because it is used where sight distance is limited or passing would be unsafe.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic. You must still check carefully and only pass when you have enough distance to do so safely.

question: As speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Looking well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turning on your headlights.,c:Changing lanes frequently.
note: As your speed increases, you cover more distance in the same amount of time, and your stopping distance grows. You must look farther ahead so you can see hazards early and have enough time and space to react smoothly and safely.

question: At a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and also watch for multiple trains.,b:Only watch for trains.,c:Only watch for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
note: At railroad crossings, you must watch for trains and also be alert for vehicles that are required to stop, such as school buses and many hazardous‑materials trucks. You should also check carefully for more than one track or train, since a second train can approach after the first has passed.

question: When driving at night, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to see and react to hazards. Use high beams when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before the turn is complete.
note: Signaling continuously through a turn clearly communicates your intentions to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Keeping the signal on until you complete the turn helps prevent sudden surprises and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: Facing a green signal while pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Make pedestrians wait until you clear the intersection.
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, so you must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding, even when your signal is green.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass, because it is considered unsafe from that direction.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Both because children have less-developed reflexes and are smaller and harder to see.,b:Because they are always following traffic rules.,c:Because they can stop more quickly than adults.
note: Children on bicycles are smaller, harder to see, and often less predictable than adults. Their reflexes and judgment are still developing, so they may swerve, stop suddenly, or enter the road unexpectedly. Give them extra space and slow down, especially near schools, parks, and residential areas.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Whenever you need to use them while moving.,b:Before you get into the car.,c:Before you start driving.
note: Before you start driving, adjust your seat, mirrors, and steering wheel so you have a clear view around the vehicle and can reach all controls comfortably. Mirrors must be set before the vehicle moves so you can monitor traffic and blind spots safely as soon as you begin to drive.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:In fog.,c:On a freeway at night.
note: Use low beam headlights whenever visibility is reduced by fog, heavy rain, snow, or mist. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams give better visibility in these conditions and reduce glare for other drivers.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must use every reasonable precaution to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when pedestrians are crossing improperly or disobeying signals. You should be prepared to slow, stop, or yield whenever necessary to prevent a collision with a pedestrian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should match what speed?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic regardless of traffic speed.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, as long as it is safe and legal. Matching the speed of traffic allows you to merge smoothly and reduces the risk of collisions caused by large speed differences.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and body functions, which reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time. This is why even small amounts of alcohol can seriously impair driving ability.

question: What should you expect when passing a row of parked vehicles?
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.,c:Assume other drivers and pedestrians will yield to you.
note: When driving past parked vehicles, leave space and be ready for doors to open, vehicles to pull out, or pedestrians to step into your lane. Expect the unexpected and adjust your speed and lane position so you can react safely if something suddenly enters your path.

question: What does an orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem is the standard slow-moving vehicle symbol. It warns that the vehicle usually travels 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or animal-drawn carts, so you should be prepared to slow down.

question: If you come upon a flooded roadway ahead, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn around and find an alternate route.,b:Check the depth and cross carefully if it seems shallow.,c:Proceed without stopping.
note: Flooded roads can hide deep water, strong currents, or road damage. Even shallow-looking water can sweep a vehicle away or cause it to stall. The safest choice is always to turn around and find another route.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and it is safe to proceed.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, then proceed only when the road is clear. On undivided roads, traffic in both directions must stop. On divided highways, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus is usually required to stop, unless state law says otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop. You must let cross or merging traffic go first if they are close enough to be a hazard, and only proceed when you can enter without forcing others to slow or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any pedestrians and vehicles with the right-of-way, and then proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Turning around and finding another route is the safest choice. Floodwater can be deeper or faster-moving than it appears, can hide holes or debris, and even a small amount of moving water can sweep a vehicle away. Never drive into a flooded roadway.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:Because distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.,b:Because the speed limit is increased at night.,c:Because there are fewer cars on the road at night.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far, and glare and darkness make it harder to judge how fast other vehicles are moving and how far away they are. Your vision is limited to the area lit by your headlights, so you must be extra cautious and adjust your speed and following distance.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you do to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Turn up the instrument panel lights.
note: In reduced visibility such as dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, you should turn on your low-beam headlights so others can see you. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not meant for driving. Headlights improve your visibility and help other drivers notice your vehicle sooner.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain posted speed to get through the water.,c:Shift into neutral while crossing.
note: If you see a deep puddle, the safest action is to avoid it if you can. Deep water can cause loss of traction, hide potholes or debris, and may damage your vehicle. If you cannot avoid water, slow down before entering and pass through it carefully, but never speed up to get through.

question: When driving in snow or ice, how should you make speed and direction changes?
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.,b:It is safe to use cruise control.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, make all speed and steering changes slowly and smoothly. Sudden acceleration, braking, or sharp turns can cause your tires to lose grip and the vehicle to skid. You should also avoid using cruise control on slippery roads so you can respond quickly to changing traction.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle equipped with airbags?
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under are safest in the back seat, especially in vehicles with front airbags. Airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure or kill a child in the front seat, even in a low‑speed crash. The back seat keeps children farther from the impact zone and the airbags, which is why most safety guidelines and laws recommend or require children to ride in the rear seats.

question: Broken yellow lines on the pavement are used for what purpose?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions, and permit passing where dashed.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is broken (dashed), it means passing is allowed when it is safe and legal to do so. Solid yellow lines generally mean no passing. White lines, not yellow, are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is actively leading the person.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and must be given the right‑of‑way at all times. Drivers must stop and remain stopped until the person has safely crossed. This applies whether or not the dog appears to be actively leading and whether or not a crossing guard is present.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, cough syrups containing codeine or antihistamines (all of the above).,c:Only alcohol.
note: Driving can be impaired by many substances, not just alcohol or illegal drugs. Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines containing codeine or certain antihistamines can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, and affect judgment. Always read medication labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: What are so-called 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Zones where you have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Areas with several car lengths between your vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck to maneuver safely.
note: ‘No‑zones’ are the large blind spots and close‑in areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you or cannot safely maneuver around you. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver probably cannot see you. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, alongside the cab on the right, and close in front—reduces the risk of collisions.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Have the pedestrian yield to you.,c:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.
note: Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog. Be prepared to stop completely and do not honk or try to wave them on; allow them to cross safely at their own pace.

question: Which is the correct method for checking blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for left lane changes and over your right shoulder for right lane changes.,b:Only turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.,c:Vehicles with two mirrors have no blind spots so you need not check over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly turn your head to look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. This head check lets you see into the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover and helps you avoid vehicles riding alongside you.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect a driver's:
options: a:Knowledge only.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reactions and affect your judgment, coordination, and ability to make safe driving decisions. Because these skills are critical for safe driving, you should never drive after drinking.

question: What does a red-painted curb mean?
options: a:Loading zone only.,b:Reserved for passenger pick-up and drop-off.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there for any reason, not even to drop off or pick up passengers or goods. This area must be kept clear at all times, often for safety or emergency access.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only your rearview mirror.
note: All vehicles have blind spots, but large trucks have much larger areas alongside and behind them where the driver cannot see other road users. Avoid lingering in a truck’s blind spots and give them extra space when passing or merging near them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror only.
note: Even with correctly adjusted mirrors, you must turn and glance over your shoulder to view areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Do not return to the lane until you can see the passed vehicle’s entire front in your rearview mirror, ensuring adequate space.

question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the radio up to stay awake.,b:Increase your speed to finish the trip sooner.,c:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
note: If fatigued, stop in a safe location and rest; drowsiness greatly increases crash risk.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and given a citation.
note: You must have evidence of financial responsibility with you whenever you drive and show it to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

question: If a lane control sign over your lane shows an arrow with the word 'only', what must you do?
options: a:Always make a lane change to reach your destination.,b:Travel only in the direction of the arrow.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow instead.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and 'only' means that lane is restricted to the movement indicated by the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting them off or causing them to brake suddenly.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you not do?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself against the back of the seat.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened, press your head firmly against the head restraint, and brace yourself against the seat. The seat belt and head restraint work together to reduce the risk of whiplash and other injuries. Never release your seat belt in a crash situation.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet road surfaces, you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Make abrupt turns.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, your tires have less grip and can start to ride on top of the water, a condition called hydroplaning. To reduce this risk, you should slow down and drive smoothly. Avoid hard braking and sudden turns, which can cause you to lose control more easily on slippery surfaces.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road, such as when hydroplaning, gently ease your foot off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or make sudden movements; braking can cause a skid. Wait until you feel the tires regain traction before slowing further or steering normally.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross and you want to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way. When you are turning and see a blind pedestrian waiting to cross, stop and wait until they have completely crossed the street. Do not give verbal instructions or try to direct them; they rely on their training, the dog, and traffic sounds to cross safely.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Drink coffee and keep driving.,b:Stop to rest or change drivers.,c:Open a window and continue driving.
note: The safest response to fatigue is to stop and rest or switch drivers; short remedies like coffee or open windows are not reliable.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window regularly.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Checking your mirrors regularly lets you know where vehicles are behind and around you so you can change lanes, slow, or stop more safely. You should glance at your mirrors frequently, not stare, and still check over your shoulder for blind spots when changing lanes.

question: If a vehicle approaches with its high beams on, what is the recommended initial response?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights.,b:Keep staring straight ahead into the glare.,c:Quickly flash your headlights one time.
note: If an oncoming driver is using high beams, you may briefly flash your headlights once to remind them to dim. If they do not, avoid looking directly at the glare; instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes.

question: A good driver should watch which areas around their vehicle?
options: a:Only the middle of the road.,b:Directly in front of the car only.,c:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and behind their vehicle. This helps you spot hazards early, judge other drivers’ actions, and leave yourself room to react by slowing, changing lanes, or stopping.

question: At what approximate speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:About 30 miles per hour.,b:About 35 miles per hour.,c:About 50 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as about 35 mph on standing water, especially with worn tires or deeper water. As speed increases, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water, greatly reducing steering and braking control.

question: If you need to use your cell phone while driving, what is best?
options: a:Stop in a safe place first before using the phone.,b:Keep all phone conversations short.,c:Use a hands-free device and drive normally.
note: Stopping in a safe place before using your phone is the safest choice. Even hands‑free use can distract your attention from the road, so you should pull over and park safely before making calls, texting, or using apps whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:If it is safe, change to the lane away from the on‑ramp to create space for entering vehicles.,b:If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to create a safe gap for entering vehicles.,c:Maintain your speed and position and let entering vehicles adjust on their own.
note: When you are already on the freeway and see vehicles entering, you should help them merge safely. If it is safe, change to the lane away from the on‑ramp to give them space. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed—usually by slightly reducing it—so there is a safe gap for them to enter. Always avoid sudden braking or lane changes that could surprise other drivers.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow for your lane, under what condition may you proceed?
options: a:If you are in the corresponding lane, the roadway is clear, and you yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only when the entire intersection is completely empty of all other traffic and pedestrians.
note: A green arrow is a protected signal for the movement it indicates. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the roadway is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What actually reduces the effects of alcohol after several beers?
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Drinking several cups of coffee.,c:Waiting several hours for the body to metabolize it.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system. Coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed up metabolism; about one hour per drink is typical.

question: If parked facing uphill where there is no curb, after setting the parking brake which way should you turn the wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels to the right toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels left toward the center of the road.
note: When parking facing uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road, and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into traffic, reducing the risk of a collision.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams at night, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Straight ahead in the center of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision and still stay oriented, shift your gaze slightly to the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using the lane line or road edge as a guide. This reduces glare while helping you maintain a safe path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, what is the safe procedure?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Slow down and just look both ways without stopping.
note: If buildings, parked cars, or other obstacles block your view at an intersection, you must treat it as a potential hazard. Come to a complete stop at the proper stopping point, then move forward slowly, inching out until you can clearly see cross traffic in both directions. Only proceed when you are sure it is safe and clear.

question: When it is very foggy, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers only.
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets in the air and create glare, which actually makes it harder to see. Use low beam headlights, and fog lights if your vehicle has them, so the light stays lower on the road and improves visibility. Always slow down and increase following distance in foggy conditions.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,b:Construction workers must yield to you.,c:You must yield to pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is painted or unmarked at an intersection. You must slow or stop to let pedestrians cross safely. Only proceed when the crosswalk is clear or when traffic signals or a crossing guard clearly direct you to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic but your light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Follow the vehicles ahead and enter the intersection.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. Enter only if there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to clear completely. If traffic ahead is stopped and you cannot get all the way through, wait behind the stop line until the intersection is clear so you do not trap cross traffic when their light turns green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When vehicles are merging into your lane on a freeway, you should help traffic flow smoothly and safely. If you can do so safely, adjust your speed or move over to create space so the merging driver can enter without sudden braking or swerving. You are not required to force them in, but cooperation reduces collisions and keeps traffic moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, you and the driver on your left arrive simultaneously. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left.,b:Whoever is signaling to turn.,c:The driver on your right (you have the right-of-way).
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. In this situation, you are to the right of the other driver, so you may proceed first after stopping. Always make sure the other driver is yielding before you go, even when you have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when clear.,b:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,c:Reduce speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic already on the highway. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge into a safe gap without stopping in the acceleration lane unless traffic or conditions force you to stop.

question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicates what?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from that lane.,c:The protection of the green arrow is ending — prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means your protected left-turn phase is ending. The green arrow will soon change, so you should prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection and can no longer stop safely, you may complete the turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign at an intersection, what is required?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other vehicles with the right-of-way before proceeding when it is safe.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Stay focused on the centerline of the road.,b:Flash your high beams.,c:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. Do not stare directly at the headlights, and do not fixate on the centerline, because both can temporarily blind you and reduce your ability to see hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If three vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. If you see a vehicle to your right, let that driver go first. This rule helps decide who goes when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane highways, slower traffic should use the right lane. If you are in the center lane and vehicles are passing you on both sides, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. Move safely to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish right-of-way.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely through.,c:Enter and wait until traffic clears.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. Only enter if you can completely clear the intersection without stopping. If traffic ahead is stopped and there is not enough room, wait behind the stop line until you can get all the way through.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending. If you are already in the intersection, complete your turn carefully. If you have not entered, prepare to stop and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when the signal changes.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your left foot for braking.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,c:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals at once and gives you better control and consistency when switching between speeding up and slowing down. Braking should be smooth and gradual, not abrupt, to maintain traction and avoid skids.

question: Why should you not use high beam headlights when driving in fog or mist?
