options: a:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,b:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine light into the tiny water droplets in the air. That light reflects back toward your eyes, creating glare and actually making it harder to see. Use low beams so the light stays lower on the road and improves your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: What type of headlights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, always use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare from moisture in the air. High beams reflect off fog, rain, or snow and can blind you with glare, making it harder to see the road and other vehicles.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination (all of the above).,b:Only reaction time.,c:Only coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect the central nervous system, which controls alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination. When these skills are reduced, you are slower to notice hazards, slower to react, and less able to control the vehicle smoothly, greatly increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, how can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:You can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:If the other driver signals for you to return.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: After passing, do not move back into your lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This shows you have created enough space in front of that vehicle to return safely without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: When driving through a work zone, what is the safest following practice?
options: a:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible to avoid delays.,b:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,c:Follow the driver in front of you closely to stay with traffic flow.
note: In work zones you should slow down, avoid tailgating, and leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead. Traffic can stop or change lanes suddenly due to workers, equipment, or lane shifts, so a larger following distance gives you more time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,b:You must stay within your lane at all times.,c:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross this line to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling. You are not required to stay in your lane at all times on such a roadway.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by only looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot cover, and large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars. Because of their size and height, trucks may not see you if you are close behind them, directly beside them, or very close in front, so you should avoid lingering in these areas.

question: How do you drive defensively?
options: a:Look only at the car directly in front of you.,b:Maintain just one car length of space ahead.,c:Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you. By keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors regularly, you can spot hazards early, anticipate what other drivers might do, and give yourself time and space to react safely.

question: Do motorcycle operators have the right to use an entire traffic lane?
options: a:Use half of a traffic lane.,b:Use a complete traffic lane.,c:Use the shoulder of a roadway.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to use a full traffic lane just like any other motor vehicle. Other drivers should not crowd them or try to share the same lane side by side, because motorcycles need the full lane for maneuvering and maintaining a safe space cushion.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the tire gently touches the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the curb will stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

question: Why should you increase following distance when driving behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because other drivers always pull behind large vehicles before passing.,b:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,c:Because you'll be caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead and may have larger blind spots. By increasing your following distance, you can see farther down the road, have more time to react, and stay out of the truck’s blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, at what point should you return to your original lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the passed vehicle's front bumper.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren and lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,b:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,c:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
note: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, continue through the intersection first. Once you are clear of the intersection, pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:For other drivers to change lanes in front of the truck.,b:For the truck driver to have enough room to slow or stop safely.,c:For other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
note: Large trucks are very heavy and need much more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver enough room to slow or stop safely if traffic changes suddenly, helping prevent rear-end collisions.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can distract you, slow your reactions, and make you take risks you normally would not take. It is safest to wait and give yourself time to calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After signaling and matching the speed of traffic on an entrance ramp, what should you do before entering the interstate?
options: a:Merge carefully into the available gap in traffic.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the entire lane to clear before merging.
note: When entering an interstate, you should use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and then merge smoothly into a safe gap. Do not assume others will yield; you must adjust to fit safely into the flow.

question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Follow closer than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Fall farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass immediately.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots directly behind them and need more distance to stop. By following farther behind than you would a passenger car, you improve your view of the road ahead and give yourself more time to react if the truck slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At traffic speeds of 50–55 mph, how can you best reduce accident risk?
options: a:Stay within that speed range and adjust to the flow.,b:Drive a few mph faster than most vehicles.,c:Drive a few mph slower than most vehicles.
note: Crashes are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or slower than surrounding traffic. As long as you stay within the posted speed limit, driving at about the same speed as nearby traffic reduces speed differences and lowers your risk of collisions.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure about your vehicle position?
options: a:Stay in the right lane as much as possible.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: When passing a motorcycle, treat it like any other vehicle and give it a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before you start to pass, do not share the lane side‑by‑side with the motorcycle, and stay fully in the passing lane until you are safely ahead and can return without crowding the rider.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what is the appropriate manner to complete the pass?
options: a:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass as slowly as possible to remain beside it longer.
note: When you pass, you should move into the passing lane, accelerate enough to pass promptly without lingering in the blind spot, and complete the maneuver safely. Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle (often its headlights) in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe following distance.

question: If you are being followed too closely (tailgated) on a two-lane road, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Apply your brakes briefly, then resume your original speed.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,c:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.
note: If someone is following too closely, do not brake suddenly or speed up. Instead, slow down gradually to increase your following distance ahead and, when safe, encourage or allow the tailgater to pass. This reduces the risk of a rear‑end collision and keeps space in front of you to react to hazards.

question: How can sudden gusts of wind affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They generally only affect very large vehicles.,b:They only create visibility problems.,c:They can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Sudden gusts of wind can push any vehicle sideways or make steering less stable, especially at highway speeds. Light vehicles, motorcycles, and high‑profile vehicles like trucks and vans are most affected, but all drivers should be prepared to adjust steering and speed when strong winds occur.

question: If an oncoming driver's bright headlights bother you at night, what is the proper response?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look directly at the headlights to judge distance.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can cause glare and reduce your ability to see. Do not look directly at the lights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide while keeping the oncoming vehicle in your peripheral vision until it passes.

question: Reaction time is slowed after:
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard all day.
note: Alcohol slows your brain and body responses, so it takes longer to notice hazards and move your foot from the gas to the brake. This means your reaction time is delayed and you need more distance to stop safely. Sleeping and working hard may cause fatigue, but the question is specifically about the clear, direct effect of drinking alcohol on reaction time.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You should use cruise control to maintain a constant speed when approaching railroad tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,c:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
note: You must always obey control devices and people directing traffic at railroad crossings. If a flagger, stop sign, or signal tells you to stop, you must come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is clearly safe. You never have the right-of-way over a train, and you should not use cruise control when approaching tracks because you may need to slow or stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a turn lane to make a left turn with oncoming traffic present, what should you do before arriving at the intersection?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be ready.,b:Signal in advance and keep your wheels straight until turning.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Before a left turn, signal well in advance and enter the proper turn lane, but keep your front wheels pointed straight until you actually begin turning. If your wheels are turned left and another vehicle hits you from behind, your car can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight helps prevent being forced into a head-on collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:If you increase your speed before the turn.,b:If traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:If traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You must yield to pedestrians and other traffic and make the turn from the proper lane into the proper lane.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:A motorcycle can stop more quickly than many vehicles.,b:Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as cars.,c:They always brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly or swerves to avoid a hazard. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles to reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what is allowed?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They must wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists are generally treated like drivers of vehicles. When making a left turn, they may move into the appropriate left lane or left‑turn lane and complete the turn like a motor vehicle, when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires that drivers:
options: a:Be constantly alert.,b:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,c:Both of the above.
note: Interstate driving involves higher speeds and heavier traffic. Drivers must stay alert to changing conditions and also be comfortable and capable of safely controlling their vehicle at freeway speeds.

question: What color and lettering do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary construction and maintenance (work zone) signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols. This color combination alerts drivers to road work and the need to slow down and use extra caution.

question: When entering a roundabout, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Only traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already in the roundabout.,c:Only crossing pedestrians.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, bicyclists, and all vehicles already circulating in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap in traffic and the crosswalks are clear.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are legally considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous.
note: On the roadway, bicycles are legally considered vehicles. Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles and must obey traffic signs, signals, and lane markings.

question: To be able to turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:On the top and bottom of the wheel.,b:Next to each other on top of the wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: Keep your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly at the 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 positions). This gives you the best leverage and control for making quick, precise turns while still being able to steer smoothly and recover the wheel after the turn.

question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Open a window to stay awake.,b:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.,c:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
note: If you feel tired while driving, the safe choice is to stop driving and rest or switch drivers. Opening a window or drinking caffeine may briefly make you feel more alert, but they do not prevent drowsy-driving crashes. Only real rest restores your ability to drive safely.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must leave a note in a secure, visible place with your name, address, and contact information, and report the collision as required by local law. This ensures the owner can reach you to handle damages properly.

question: What is true about driving through roadwork zones?
options: a:Fines are the same as under normal traffic conditions.,b:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone.' ,c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: In roadwork zones you must slow down, obey posted work-zone speed limits, and be prepared to stop. The phrase “Slow for the Cone Zone” reminds drivers to reduce speed and drive cautiously to protect road workers and other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, how should you enter an interstate?
options: a:Use the shoulder to reach traffic speed.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up.,c:Wait for a safe gap in traffic, then accelerate to merge.
note: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, you must wait for a safe gap in traffic, then accelerate firmly on the ramp so you are close to the speed of traffic as you merge. Do not use the shoulder to gain speed, and do not force your way in without a safe opening.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line in the center of a two‑way road separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed from either direction when it is safe. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough clear distance before crossing the line to pass.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning in wet conditions, what should you do?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. The best prevention is to slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly so your tires can maintain traction and channel water away.

question: The traditional mirror setting is:
options: a:Shows the edge of the vehicle in the side mirrors.,b:Is the best choice for minimizing blind spots in all situations.,c:May be appropriate for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight areas.
note: In the traditional mirror setting, you can see the side of your own vehicle in both side mirrors. This can reduce blind spots less effectively than the enhanced setting, but it may be helpful for large vehicles, towing, or backing in tight spaces because it gives a clear view of the vehicle’s sides and trailer alignment.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, what should you do before going down steep hills?
options: a:Pump brakes continuously to keep them from freezing.,b:Maintain close following distance behind other vehicles.,c:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
note: On snow or ice, using engine braking by shifting to a lower gear before going down a steep hill helps control your speed and reduces the need for heavy braking, which can cause skids. Increase your following distance and brake gently; if you do not have ABS, use light, repeated braking rather than a hard, continuous press.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,b:Continue ahead because the motorist has the right-of-way.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Slow or stop as needed and wait until pedestrians have fully crossed your lane and it is clearly safe before proceeding. Never drive around pedestrians in a crosswalk, even if you are in a hurry.

question: If your tires begin to lose traction due to water on the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,c:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.
note: When your tires hydroplane, they ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, so braking or turning suddenly can cause a skid. The safest response is to ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and let the vehicle slow down gradually until the tires regain traction. Avoid hard braking or sharp steering inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Assume all drivers automatically obey right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not give you the right to cause a collision. A safe driver never assumes others will follow the rules and is always prepared to yield if it will prevent a crash. Being willing to give up your turn is an important defensive driving habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the likely effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time.,b:Helps maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious injury or death.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to react and increases the distance needed to stop. In a crash, higher speed means more force on your body and your vehicle, which greatly increases the chance of serious injury or death. Even if speeding seems to save a little time, the safety risk is much greater.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How is a crosswalk defined?
options: a:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the road set aside for pedestrians to cross. It can be marked with painted lines or be an unmarked extension of the sidewalk across an intersection. Drivers must watch for people in crosswalks and yield to them as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
note: The shoulder is not a travel lane. Using it to pass is generally illegal and very dangerous because other drivers do not expect a vehicle there and may pull onto the shoulder in an emergency or to turn. You must stay in a proper lane when passing and only pass where it is legal and safe.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates what about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the side of the broken line may cross the center line to pass, and only when it is safe. Traffic on the side of the solid yellow line must not cross the line to pass.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, you should use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve visibility without as much glare.

question: What does a broken yellow line between lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow line between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough space, and return to your lane before any oncoming vehicle gets close.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio.,b:Always keep your eyes focused straight ahead.,c:Know what is happening around your vehicle at all times.
note: The best way to avoid dangerous situations is to stay aware of everything around your vehicle—ahead, behind, and to the sides. By constantly scanning and checking mirrors, you can spot hazards early and have more time to react safely.

question: Which action is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,c:Proceeding to the next exit if you miss yours.
note: On interstates, you should always signal before changing lanes, keep slower traffic to the right, and continue to the next exit if you miss yours. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe because other drivers cannot anticipate your movement and may not have time to adjust.

question: What does a red arrow pointing to the right on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Do not turn in that direction until the arrow changes to green.,b:You may turn right after coming to a complete stop.,c:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped for that specific turning movement. You may not turn in the direction of the red arrow until it changes to green or you get a green light that allows that turn.

question: Blue roadway signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas and hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage and directional distances to locations.
note: Blue signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas, food, lodging, and hospitals so drivers can find needed facilities while traveling.

question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not using a phone.,c:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked. You must slow or stop to let pedestrians cross safely and only proceed when the crosswalk is clear.

question: With a Class C driver license you may operate which of these vehicles?
options: a:Any motor vehicle regardless of size.,b:A vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 26,001 pounds.,c:A vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating over 26,001 pounds.
note: A standard Class C license allows you to drive most regular passenger vehicles and light trucks with a gross vehicle weight rating under 26,001 pounds. Heavier vehicles usually require a commercial driver license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what important check should you make?
options: a:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,b:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, you must quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. This area cannot be seen in your mirrors and may hide another vehicle or motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your position in traffic, including when you pull toward the curb to park and when you leave the curb to re-enter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions so they can react safely.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness only.,b:Coordination only.,c:Both alertness and coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness, slow your reactions, and affect coordination and judgment. Because both alertness and coordination are impaired, your ability to steer, brake, and respond to hazards is significantly reduced even at relatively low doses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian?
options: a:When the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk, and you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians crossing the street whenever they are close enough to be in danger.,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when they are crossing at a signalized intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and at intersections. In many states, you must also stop or yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway when they are close enough to be in danger, even outside a crosswalk. Always be prepared to yield to pedestrians to prevent collisions.

question: How does a BAC of 0.02 percent affect crash risk?
options: a:It can roughly double your chances of having an accident.,b:It has no effect on your driving.,c:It will not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system increases crash risk. Around a 0.02% BAC, studies show your chance of being in a crash can be about double that of a sober driver because your judgment, vision, and reaction time are already affected.

question: If visibility is less than 100 feet because of weather (rain, snow, dust, smoke, fog), what is the maximum safe speed?
options: a:40 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: You must always be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. If visibility is under 100 feet, a speed around 20 mph or less is safer; at 30 mph you travel about 44 feet per second and may not have enough distance to see a hazard and stop in time on a wet or slick road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never — it confuses other drivers.,b:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.,c:Often, even at controlled intersections.
note: You must never insist on your right-of-way if doing so could cause a crash. Even when you are legally entitled to go first, you should yield if another driver does not yield or if yielding will help prevent a collision.

question: When will your driver's license expire?
options: a:It renews automatically without any action from you.,b:It never expires.,c:On your birthday in the expiration year shown on your license.
note: In many states, including Kansas, a standard driver’s license expires on the holder’s birthday in the expiration year shown on the license. It does not renew automatically and it does not last forever; you must renew it before or by that date to keep driving legally.

question: When you encounter orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Change lanes and keep your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce speed.,c:Maintain speed and ignore the signs.
note: Orange signs and cones indicate a work zone. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and watch for workers, equipment, and lane shifts. Speeding or ignoring work-zone warnings is dangerous and often carries higher fines.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching from behind on a city street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.,c:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down only if other cars do.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: If smoke heavily covers the road ahead, how should you respond?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and continue slowly.,b:Reduce speed, move far right, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on high beams and continue.
note: In heavy smoke or similar zero-visibility conditions, you should slow down, move as far right as you safely can, and stop completely off the roadway if possible. Using high beams or continuing to drive in near-zero visibility greatly increases the risk of a collision.

question: How can drowsiness affect driving?
options: a:Help you to be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment and performance.
note: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces alertness, and harms your judgment, much like alcohol. A tired driver may not notice hazards in time or may make poor decisions, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:So other drivers can see your vehicle.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, visibility is reduced. Turning on your low‑beam headlights makes it easier for other drivers to see you, which helps prevent collisions. In many states, if your windshield wipers are on, your headlights are legally required.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. The gate and flashing lights mean a train is approaching or nearby, and trains cannot stop quickly. Wait until the gates are fully raised and you can clearly see that the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, from which lane should you start the turn?
options: a:The lane in the center of the road.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane as long as it is safe.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, start from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps you in the proper lane, avoids cutting across traffic, and matches how other drivers expect you to turn.

question: If you must park where vehicles do not usually park, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park with your reverse lights on.
note: If you must park where vehicles do not usually park, make sure your vehicle can be seen by drivers coming from any direction. Good visibility reduces the chance that another driver will be surprised by your parked vehicle and hit it.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait for them to lift.,c:Slow down and drive around the gates.
note: At railroad crossings with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop before the gate, never drive around or under it, and wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing before proceeding. Trains can approach faster and more quietly than expected, and going around the gates is illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you react?
options: a:Slow down and allow the other driver to return to the driving lane safely.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: If another driver is passing you, even in a no‑passing zone, you should help avoid a collision by slowing slightly and allowing them space to return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or block them. Your goal is to reduce risk, even when the other driver is making an unsafe or illegal maneuver.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, how should you drive?
options: a:Beep your horn to warn the child.,b:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your path. You should slow down, be ready to brake, and give them extra space, always expecting the unexpected rather than assuming they are fully in control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you look?
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again because traffic from the left is closer to you. Also scan ahead and across the intersection for vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists. This pattern helps you detect hazards that may have appeared since your first glance.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, what should drivers do?
options: a:Only check the left outside mirror.,b:Look over the appropriate shoulder (left or right).,c:Only check the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you intend to move toward to ensure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but see no gap, how should you proceed on the ramp?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and be prepared to yield until there is a safe gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp, be prepared to stop if needed, and wait for a safe opening to accelerate and merge.,c:Maintain your ramp speed and force drivers to yield.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should use the ramp to adjust your speed so you can merge smoothly into traffic. If there is no gap, slow down on the ramp and be prepared to stop if necessary, then accelerate when a safe opening appears. Never force your way in or stop suddenly in the lane of freeway traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane while many vehicles are passing you on the right and the driver behind wishes to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.,b:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: The left lane is generally for passing or faster traffic. If vehicles are passing you on the right and a driver behind you wants to go faster, you should safely move to the right lane when possible so traffic can flow smoothly.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol's impairing effects from your system?
options: a:Wait.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol and lower your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, cold showers, food, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not reduce impairment or make you safe to drive.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed (broken) yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the dashed line, and prohibited for traffic on the side with the solid line. Any passing must still be done only when it is safe.

question: What is the correct approach when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and drive with extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear the zone sooner.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often have changing traffic patterns, workers close to moving vehicles, and equipment entering the roadway. You should slow down, obey all signs and flaggers, and drive with extra caution to protect workers and other road users.

question: What should you avoid doing when passing through a construction zone?
options: a:Driving with extra caution.,b:Slowing down to watch workers or incidents (“rubbernecking”).,c:Passing carefully and remaining alert.
note: In construction zones you must avoid rubbernecking—slowing down just to look at workers, equipment, or crashes. This behavior distracts you from the road, surprises drivers behind you, and often causes rear‑end collisions and traffic jams. Instead, reduce speed as required, stay focused on the lane and signs, and pass through the work zone smoothly and attentively.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels and causes a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice or snow, continuous hard braking can cause your wheels—especially the front wheels—to lock. When the front wheels are locked, the vehicle will slide straight ahead and you can lose the ability to steer around hazards. To maintain control, slow down early, brake gently and progressively, and allow extra following distance. If your vehicle has ABS, apply firm, steady pressure and let the system prevent wheel lockup.

question: When the roadway is wet or icy, what action should you take?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive the posted speed.,c:Speed up to clear slippery spots.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy roads greatly reduce traction, which means your tires grip the road less and your stopping distance increases. You should reduce your speed so you have more time to react and can brake and steer smoothly without skidding. Driving at or above the posted speed on slippery roads is unsafe, even if it is within the legal limit.

question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go; you do not remain stopped the entire time it is flashing.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Drive closely behind the truck in bad weather because it can see farther ahead.,c:Stay about one car length behind so the truck driver can see you.
note: Large trucks need more time and distance to stop, and they block more of your view of the road ahead. You should follow them at a greater distance than you would a passenger car so you can see around the truck, react to hazards, and stop safely if it brakes suddenly. Tailgating a truck puts you in its blind spots and leaves you no room to avoid a collision.

question: When must vehicles stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights remain stopped?
options: a:Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:Until all students are off the bus.,c:Until the stop arm is retracted only.
note: Motorists must stop until the bus turns off its red lights, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven under which conditions?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed only when conditions are ideal: good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and no hazards. In rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or when visibility is reduced, you are required to slow down below the posted limit to a speed that is safe for the conditions.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are harder to see, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow down only when passing a motorcycle.,b:Share the same lane with a motorcycle to keep it visible.,c:Make frequent visual checks for motorcycles and similar vehicles.
note: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can easily be hidden in blind spots or blend into traffic. Drivers should make frequent, deliberate visual checks—using mirrors and turning their head to check blind spots—especially before changing lanes, turning, or entering an intersection. Never share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle; they are entitled to a full lane.

question: Which windows should you clear of snow, frost, and ice before driving?
options: a:All windows.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must be able to see through all windows and mirrors; remove snow, ice, and frost from all of them prior to driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After passing on the left, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) clearly in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle. Always signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and then return to the lane smoothly without cutting the other driver off.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their bright headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, shift your gaze toward the right edge of your lane and use the right side of the road as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you avoid being temporarily blinded while still keeping enough of the roadway in view.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train.,b:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,c:Both of the above.
note: After a train passes, always check carefully for a second train that may be coming on another track, and do not proceed until all warning devices—such as flashing lights and lowered gates—have fully stopped and the gates are completely raised. Trains can be very close and quiet, so you must confirm the crossing is completely clear before moving.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Use the brakes lightly and slow down gradually.,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: If a tire suddenly goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have good control and your speed has dropped, brake gently. Sudden or hard braking can cause you to lose control, especially with a flat tire.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what?
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem stopped for no reason.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Stop, listen, and then proceed cautiously.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, always scan to the left and right sides of your vehicle to see if pedestrians, cyclists, or other vehicles are entering your path. Vehicles may be stopped ahead of you to let someone cross, so you must look to the sides instead of just straight ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Cross the centerline in an intersection.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in an intersection; wait until you have fully passed through. When changing lanes, always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and make sure no one else is moving into the same lane before you steer over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: You should never change lanes abruptly or spontaneously. Safe lane changes require signaling in advance, checking mirrors and blind spots, and moving over smoothly only when the lane is clear. Looking over your shoulder and checking for other vehicles are essential safety steps, not behaviors to avoid.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If another driver is following too closely (tailgating), you should increase the space in front of your vehicle. This larger following distance gives you more time to brake gradually and reduces the chance of a rear-end collision if you must slow or stop.

question: When driving in fog, which lights and actions are appropriate?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights and maintain normal speed.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: In fog, always slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe location, turn on your hazard lights, and wait until conditions improve.

question: Why is using a cellphone while driving distracting?
options: a:Because it occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:Because it makes the driver concern about call costs.,c:Because it draws other drivers' attention away.
note: Using a cellphone while driving is dangerous because it can take your hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your mind off driving. This combination greatly increases the risk of missing hazards and being involved in a crash.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should occupants still do?
options: a:Wear seat belts behind the back only.,b:Wear seat belts at all times.,c:Not wear seat belts.
note: Even in vehicles with airbags, all occupants must wear seat belts at all times. Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you effectively.

question: When driving in fog, which lights are best to use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and creates less glare. High beams reflect off water droplets in fog, rain, or snow and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Four-way flashers are for stopped or very slow-moving vehicles, not for normal driving in fog.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Always use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear); also turn your front wheels so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.,b:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.
note: Whenever you park on a hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park" (or in gear for a manual). This helps keep the vehicle from rolling if the primary brakes fail. In addition, you must turn the front wheels so that if the vehicle does roll, it will roll toward the curb or edge of the road and away from traffic: turn wheels away from the curb when facing uphill with a curb, and toward the curb or road edge when facing downhill or when there is no curb.

question: If you encounter animals standing near the roadway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Swerve quickly into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: When animals are near or on the roadway, slow down and be ready to stop. Animals can move suddenly into your path, so reducing speed gives you more time and space to react safely. Do not swerve sharply or speed up, because that can cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: You should never enter an intersection unless you are sure you can clear it completely. Even with a green light, if traffic ahead is stopped and you cannot get all the way through, you must wait. Blocking an intersection can prevent cross traffic from moving and can result in a citation in many jurisdictions.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing mid-block instead of using a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:You must slow down and stop if necessary to avoid hitting them.,b:You do not have to avoid them because they are crossing illegally.,c:You should honk and continue driving at the same speed.
note: You must always drive in a way that avoids hitting pedestrians, even when they are crossing illegally. If pedestrians are in the roadway, slow down and stop if necessary to let them pass safely. After they clear your path, they are required to yield to vehicles, but you are still responsible for preventing a collision.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Proceed cautiously without stopping.,b:Expect the light to turn green soon.,c:Treat it the same as a stop sign and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When parking uphill on a road with a curb, how should your front wheels be turned?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Which statement best describes the mindset of defensive drivers?
options: a:They know other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road, anticipate possible mistakes by others, and are ready to react. They do not assume other drivers will always follow the rules.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what is the recommended way to slow the vehicle?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
note: In a tire blowout, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Use the brakes lightly only after you have good control and your speed has dropped.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, and it is clear that no children are crossing.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Sound your horn whenever children are present.
note: A school crossing sign means children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully on both sides of the street, and be prepared to stop if children are in or near the crosswalk.

question: What should you do when prescribed a medication that may affect driving?
options: a:Have someone follow you home.,b:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about its effects before driving.,c:Open the window and drive more slowly.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medication may affect your driving before you drive after taking it.

question: When preparing to make a left turn at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.,b:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:Pedestrians who have a 'Walk' signal or are in the crosswalk.
note: When turning left, you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk (or who have the WALK signal), as well as to oncoming traffic that has the right‑of‑way. Pedestrians in the crosswalk have priority over turning vehicles, so you must wait until they have safely crossed before completing your turn.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. They are typically white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Braking hard or suddenly.,b:Braking lightly.,c:Steering smoothly in the direction you want to go.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, slamming or even normal braking can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Use brakes only very gently and only if your vehicle has ABS and you are trained to use firm, steady pressure.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,b:Traffic control devices that are obscured.,c:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the mirrors.
note: Blind spots are the areas around your vehicle that you cannot see by using your mirrors alone. To check them, you must quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Not turn the steering wheel.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the right.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer in the same direction that the rear of the vehicle is skidding. If the rear moves left, gently steer left to help straighten the vehicle. Avoid sudden braking or jerky steering, especially if you do not have ABS.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, what is the best way to avoid vehicles merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Maintain speed and position in the right lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when traffic allows.,c:Slow down significantly.
note: On highways, it is safer and more courteous to move out of the right lane when you see vehicles entering from on-ramps, if traffic allows. Changing to the left lane gives merging drivers space and helps prevent sudden braking or conflicts in the right lane.

question: Construction zone signs are typically what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Construction and work-zone signs are temporary warning signs. They are usually orange with black symbols or lettering and are often diamond-shaped, though some may be rectangular for specific information or directions.

question: What is the correct technique when backing up?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal.,c:Look through the rear window while backing up.
note: When backing up, you should turn your body and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Do not rely only on mirrors or cameras, and keep your foot ready on the brake so you can stop quickly if needed.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, how should you re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,b:Stop immediately and remain stopped.,c:Wait until it is safe, reduce speed, then gradually re-enter the roadway.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, stay off the gas, and gently slow down. Do not jerk the steering wheel back onto the road. Once the car is under control and traffic is clear, gradually steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield, and proceed carefully. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and any vehicles that may not yield before you enter the intersection.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:Privilege, not a right.,b:Requirement.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: In all U.S. states, driving is considered a privilege granted by the government, not a guaranteed right. You must meet licensing requirements and can lose this privilege if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you creating a hazard, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Honk and then brake firmly.,b:Swerve into the adjacent lane immediately.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: When a vehicle cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator. This increases your following distance smoothly and reduces the need for sudden braking or swerving, which can cause loss of control or collisions with vehicles beside or behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Use mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror only.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This combination ensures you see vehicles that mirrors alone might miss so you can merge safely into the flow of traffic.

question: If dust or smoke limits your vision, what lights should you turn on?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: When dust, smoke, or similar conditions reduce visibility, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights. This makes it easier for you to see and, more importantly, helps other drivers see your vehicle. Parking lights or emergency flashers alone are not sufficient or appropriate for driving in these conditions.

question: Which behavior disrupts the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Slowing down just to look at a collision or something unusual on the road is called rubbernecking. It disrupts the smooth flow of traffic, creates sudden slowdowns, and increases the risk of rear‑end crashes and additional collisions. Avoid unnecessary slowing to look at incidents so traffic can keep moving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must always obey a police officer or authorized person directing traffic, even if traffic signals say something different. You are also required to stop at a steady or flashing red traffic light or signal. Because both situations require a stop, the correct choice is that both are conditions where you must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,c:Passing cars.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, including motorcycles and bicycles. Wait until there is a safe gap before turning. Failing to yield when turning left is a common cause of serious collisions.

question: Who must drivers obey when directing traffic at a construction site?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Flaggers (signal persons) in construction or work zones are authorized to direct traffic and must be obeyed just like traffic signals or police officers. Their instructions help protect workers and drivers by safely guiding vehicles through changing or hazardous conditions in the work area.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Many medicines can affect your driving, not just illegal drugs. Both prescription and over‑the‑counter medications can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist; if a drug can make you less alert, you should not drive after taking it.

question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should always be done gradually and carefully. Signal first, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and move smoothly into the new lane only when there is enough space. Sudden or frequent lane changes increase the risk of a collision.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm and ease off the accelerator. Sudden braking can make the skid worse. Steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go and make smooth, gentle corrections until you regain traction.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Drive on its right side while on curves and hills.,b:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,c:Avoid driving beside it for extended periods.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving beside them for long periods because the driver may not see you and could change lanes or turn into your path. Pass promptly and safely, and don’t linger next to a large vehicle.

question: What is the likely consequence of continually passing other cars on a two-lane road?
options: a:You will increase your chances of being in a collision.,b:You will get to your destination much more quickly and safely.,c:You will help prevent traffic congestion.
note: On two‑lane roads, every pass puts you into the oncoming traffic lane, which greatly increases your risk of a head‑on collision. Continually passing other cars exposes you to more danger and saves little time. Pass only when it is legal, necessary, and clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:You must yield only to vehicles on your right.,b:You should slow down but never stop.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let cross traffic and any pedestrians go first if they are close enough to be a hazard or require you to change speed or direction. You only proceed when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: If your car starts skidding out of control, what should you do with the brakes?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: If your vehicle is skidding, stay off the brakes. Braking can make the skid worse by locking the wheels and reducing your ability to steer. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until you regain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a green arrow, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection. Do not enter the intersection until it is clear and safe to complete your turn.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line allow?
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass.,b:Drivers in either direction may pass.,c:Drivers next to the solid line may pass.
note: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, only drivers on the side with the broken line may pass if it is safe and legal. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

question: Which factor listed affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: A person’s weight affects how alcohol is absorbed and how concentrated it becomes in the blood. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a heavier person after drinking the same amount. Other factors include biological sex, how much and how quickly alcohol is consumed, and whether there is food in the stomach.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single broken white lane line mean when driving on a highway?
options: a:You may cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:You cannot cross it to pass.,c:You may only cross it from the left lane.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: If you expect to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Applying your brakes.
note: If you expect to be hit from the rear, keep both hands firmly on the steering wheel so you can maintain control of the vehicle. Press your head and back against the head restraint and seat to reduce whiplash, and be ready to brake to avoid being pushed into another vehicle. Do not let go of the steering wheel.

question: If poor weather makes it hard to see, what driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Speed up to reach your destination faster.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: In poor weather or low visibility, you should slow down and increase your following distance. More space in front of you gives extra time to see hazards and stop safely on slippery or wet roads.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:You may not proceed until it turns green.,b:Treat it like a stop sign, coming to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Speed up slightly to crest the hill.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed without adjustments.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, your view of what is ahead is limited. You should control your speed so you can stop if necessary for stalled vehicles, slow traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards that may be just beyond the crest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels toward the side of the road or the curb.
note: When you park facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll toward the curb and stop instead of rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's instructions and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer tells you to go through a red light, you must follow the officer’s instructions, proceeding carefully as directed.

question: What does an instructional permit allow you to do?
options: a:Operate a motor vehicle while supervised by a licensed driver, following your state’s age and experience requirements.,b:Operate a motor vehicle without supervision.,c:Only observe another driver operating a vehicle.
note: An instructional (learner’s) permit lets you drive only when supervised by a properly licensed adult seated beside you. Many states require this supervising driver to be at least 21 and to have at least one year of driving experience, but the exact age and experience requirements can vary by state, so you must follow your own state’s rules.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what speed should you maintain?
options: a:Keep instrument panel lights bright so others can see you.,b:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights to see further.
note: At night you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights and ensures you have enough time to react to hazards in the illuminated area.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are needed to begin affecting your driving?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Even one alcoholic drink can slow your reaction time, reduce judgment, and affect coordination. Because there is no completely safe amount of alcohol before driving, you should avoid driving after drinking at all.

question: You exit the freeway onto a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Wait until in the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
note: You should slow to a safe speed before entering a downhill curve. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding, especially on a downgrade, and you may not have enough time to react to hazards you can’t yet see.

question: Which statement about drinking and driving is correct?
options: a:Being under the legal BAC means your driving is not impaired.,b:If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.,c:Alcohol affects judgment, which is essential for safe driving.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, reaction time, and coordination, all of which are critical for safe driving. Even if your BAC is below the legal limit or you feel fine, your driving can still be impaired and you can be unsafe behind the wheel.

question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
