options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield if another road user does not yield the right‑of‑way.

question: What should you do at night regarding following distance?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night you should increase your following distance so you have more time to see and react to hazards with reduced visibility and possible glare. More space gives you a better safety margin if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Make eye contact then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Even if no marked crosswalk exists, yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and let them finish crossing safely.

question: What color are most traffic control devices used specifically in construction and maintenance zones?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Orange.
note: Most signs, cones, and barriers used in construction and maintenance zones are orange. This bright color alerts drivers to changing road conditions and the presence of workers so they can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop on its own.
note: With ABS (anti-lock braking system), you should press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup and maintain steering control, especially on slippery surfaces like snow or ice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, which should you not do?
options: a:Continue on and find another route.,b:Proceed to the next exit and return to your intended exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, never back up on the road or shoulder. This is extremely dangerous and illegal. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route that takes you back to your intended exit.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Staring at the road directly in front of your vehicle at all times.,b:Using your high beams in fog.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: Safe drivers scan the road ahead and check their mirrors frequently—about every two to five seconds—to stay aware of surrounding traffic. You should not stare only at the area directly in front of your vehicle, and you should avoid using high beams in fog because they reflect off the moisture and reduce visibility.

question: Which statement is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:All large trucks have air brakes that allow quick stops.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles, especially when fully loaded. They are not more maneuverable, and not all trucks have air brakes, so you should never assume they can stop quickly.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating high-fat foods.,b:Time.,c:Drinking caffeine.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by food, coffee, cold showers, or any other method.

question: What message does a 'No passing zone' sign convey?
options: a:To speed up slightly to clear the zone.,b:That it is not safe to pass in the indicated area.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign means it is illegal and unsafe to pass other vehicles in that area, usually because of limited visibility, curves, hills, or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you take to check for other vehicles?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot for vehicles you cannot see in the mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what is required?
options: a:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should always yield to you.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when there is a safe gap and any required signal or green arrow allows the movement.

question: Approaching a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, what action is required?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Stop until the person is well away from your path.,c:Honk your horn as you proceed.
note: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must stop and remain stopped until the person has safely crossed and is clear of your path. Do not honk or drive around them.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use four-way flashers.,c:Use low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which of the following?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:Overtaking cars.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right. The oncoming vehicles have the right-of-way because they are continuing through the intersection, while you are crossing their path to turn left.

question: Which statement about driving slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:Driving speed does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly and may encourage risky passing. You should generally drive at or near the speed of surrounding traffic, within the posted speed limit and adjusted for conditions.

question: Any concentration of alcohol acts as what type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant. It slows the central nervous system, reducing alertness, coordination, and reaction time. Even small amounts can affect your ability to judge distances, react to hazards, and control your vehicle safely.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked ones.,b:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than oncoming vehicles.,c:Follow a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on the left and parked cars on the right, steer a middle course between them. This gives you the greatest possible space on both sides, reducing the chance of sideswiping a parked car or colliding with an oncoming vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,b:Assume the other driver will give you room to return to your lane.,c:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
note: When passing, never assume other drivers will create space for you to return to your lane. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear distance ahead and behind in the lane you are entering so you can move back without forcing anyone to slow or swerve. Always plan your pass so you can complete it safely on your own, without relying on the actions of other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what checks should you perform?
options: a:Check the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,c:Slow down and change lanes immediately.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may not appear in your mirrors. Only change lanes when the lane is clear and you can move over smoothly and safely.

question: Which is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,b:Both tailgating other vehicles and failing to watch for workers.,c:Following another vehicle too closely (tailgating).
note: In work zones, both tailgating and failing to watch for workers or equipment are dangerous. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and stay alert for sudden stops, lane shifts, and workers near the roadway. Giving yourself extra space and attention helps prevent crashes in these high‑risk areas.

question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard right before the curve.
note: Before entering a curve, reduce your speed so you can drive through it smoothly and under control. Most of your braking should be done before the curve, while your tires are straight. Entering a curve too fast and braking hard inside the curve can cause skidding or loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer orders you to stop even though the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s instructions even if they conflict with traffic lights, signs, or lane markings. The officer’s directions control the intersection and are intended to keep everyone safe in that situation.

question: How is a 'distraction' while driving defined?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your mind, eyes, or hands away from the driving task. This includes things like texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of the road. Any diversion of attention from driving increases crash risk.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt only.,b:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers have buckled theirs.,c:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts only.
note: Before starting the engine, you should always buckle your own safety belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. Making this a habit ensures everyone is protected from the moment the vehicle begins to move.

question: What can you do to help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone to stay calm while driving.,b:Use your horn frequently to remind others to yield.,c:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes.
note: To help reduce road rage, drive predictably and communicate clearly. Always signal before changing lanes or turning so other drivers know what you intend to do. This reduces surprises, misunderstandings, and conflicts that can lead to aggressive driving.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: When following another vehicle at night, use low beam headlights. High beams can shine into the mirrors of the vehicle ahead and blind or distract that driver, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may turn after coming to a complete stop.,b:Traffic in the indicated lane may not proceed in that direction.,c:You may proceed in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane must stop and may not proceed in the direction of the arrow until a green arrow or green light appears. Treat it like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at posted speed when the signal turns yellow, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution and do not speed up.

question: Which type of road surface is most likely to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air circulates above and below the surface, causing them to lose heat faster than regular roadways. Even if the main road looks wet, a bridge can be icy, so reduce speed and avoid sudden moves.

question: When following a motorcycle, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Be ready to use your horn.,c:Allow a larger following distance (at least 3–4 seconds).
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can stop or swerve more quickly than cars. Leave at least a 3–4 second following distance so you have enough time to react if the rider slows, stops, or falls. More space is safer in bad weather or at higher speeds.

question: Where are truck blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the cab only.,b:On both sides near the cab and along the sides of the trailer, and directly behind the trailer.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots ("no-zones") along both sides, directly behind the trailer, and sometimes directly in front. If you cannot see the truck driver’s face in their side mirror, they likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop on the entrance ramp before entering.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to find a gap.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, signal, and choose a safe gap. Merge smoothly into the nearest lane without stopping unless traffic or conditions make it impossible to merge safely.

question: When must safety belts be worn?
options: a:Only when driving long distances.,b:Do not need to be worn if airbags are present.,c:Must be worn at all times in a moving vehicle.
note: Safety belts must be worn by drivers and passengers whenever the vehicle is moving. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash, and airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them.

question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions?
options: a:Apply brakes immediately when the car starts to skid.,b:Drive at a speed appropriate for dry, ideal conditions.,c:Slow down in wet conditions to maintain better control.
note: To avoid hydroplaning, you should slow down in the rain, especially when water is pooling on the road. Lower speeds help your tires maintain contact with the pavement so you keep steering and braking control. Always adjust your speed below what you would use in ideal, dry conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into highway traffic, what should you do to safely enter a gap?
options: a:Check behind you and to the side, including your blind spot, and also watch the traffic ahead in the lane you are entering.,b:Speed up and expect other vehicles to yield to you.,c:Watch only the traffic behind the gap you want to enter.
note: When merging, you must check traffic behind and beside you, including your blind spots, and also watch the traffic in front of you in the lane you are entering. This lets you judge the speed and position of vehicles in the gap and merge smoothly without forcing others to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Increase your speed to avoid causing an accident.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping in the middle of the intersection can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use both the lap belt and the shoulder belt.
note: With a two-part belt system, always wear both the lap and shoulder belts. The lap belt should fit low over your hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the middle of your chest and shoulder. Using both together keeps you better restrained and reduces the chance of serious injury.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Driving slowly.,b:The number of passengers in the vehicle.,c:Erratic and improper lane changes.
note: Aggressive drivers often follow too closely, speed, and make sudden, unsafe lane changes or other risky maneuvers. Erratic and improper lane changes are a clear sign of aggressive driving, and you should avoid engaging with such drivers and give them space.

question: If approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,c:Remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:Your wheels should not be pointed straight ahead when waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on level roadway with no curb.
note: When waiting to make a left turn, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually begin the turn. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, you turn your wheels so that if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic or into the curb.

question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle carefully.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have finished crossing.,c:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.
note: You must not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield when an emergency vehicle uses siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Stop immediately, even if in an intersection.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and flashing lights, you must pull as close as you safely can to the right edge or curb and stop, staying clear of any intersection. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into any available lane.,b:Turn into the first (closest) lane of the one-way street.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must enter the first legal lane available, which is the lane closest to you on the one-way street. This keeps your path short, predictable, and prevents you from cutting across multiple lanes where you could collide with traffic already in those lanes.

question: If the road is slippery, what following distance should you maintain?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and your stopping distance increases. You should leave more space than usual between you and the vehicle ahead so you have enough time and distance to brake gently and avoid skidding if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, always use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and help you see without creating as much glare. High beams reflect off water droplets or fog in the air, bouncing light back at you and actually making it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve.,b:When there is a broken line next to your lane.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.
note: You may pass another vehicle only where passing is allowed and it is safe. A broken center line next to your lane means you are permitted to pass if you have enough clear distance ahead. You must not pass on hills, curves, or where there is a solid line next to your lane, because your view of oncoming traffic is limited or passing is specifically prohibited.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates what?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign only.
note: A pentagon-shaped sign (five-sided, point up) is used for school zones and school crossings. It alerts you that children may be present near the roadway and that you should slow down, watch carefully for pedestrians, and obey any posted school speed limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not allowed?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with 500 feet clear in both directions.
note: U‑turns are illegal and unsafe where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on or near curves and hills. You must have a clear view and enough distance in both directions before turning. In many states, U‑turns are allowed in places like parking lots or on straight roads when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs or markings.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:Yes; driving slowly is a defensive driving technique in all situations.,b:No; driving too slowly can block traffic and be unsafe.,c:Yes; it is always safer to drive slower than other traffic.
note: You should drive at a speed that is safe for conditions, not simply slower than everyone else. Driving much slower than the normal flow can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing crash risk. In poor weather or heavy traffic, reduce speed as needed, but do not block or disrupt the normal, safe flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is prohibited when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Lane changes should be made before or after intersections, not while you are inside them. Changing lanes in an intersection can surprise other drivers and create conflicts with turning or crossing traffic. Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder for blind spots before changing lanes, and complete the maneuver outside the intersection.

question: Which area is most likely to stay icy longer after snow or rain?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A shaded area of the road
note: Shaded areas of the road receive less sunlight, so ice forms sooner and melts later there than on open, sunny stretches. Bridges, overpasses, and tree‑covered sections can stay icy even when the rest of the road looks clear, so reduce speed and be especially cautious in those spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which speed should you travel at under varying conditions?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:At the speed of the vehicles immediately around you.
note: You must adjust your speed to match road, traffic, and weather conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. The speed limit is the maximum allowed in ideal conditions, not a target speed. Slow down when visibility is poor, roads are wet or icy, or traffic is heavy, while still keeping with the safe flow of traffic.

question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Slow down to no more than 10 mph.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped. You may not pass the bus or move again until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted, because children may be crossing the road.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They are not affected by speed.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:They increase as speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both stopping distance and crash severity increase. You need more distance to perceive, react, and brake to a stop, and the force of impact in a crash rises sharply with speed, making serious injury or death more likely.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When there isn't room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks. If traffic or an obstruction would leave you stopped on the tracks, you must stop and wait before the crossing until you can drive all the way across safely.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their mirrors.,c:Because large trucks travel at higher speeds than cars.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop. If you cut in front of them and brake suddenly, they may not be able to stop in time, greatly increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to guide traffic safely through or around construction areas and to keep vehicles out of hazardous zones. They protect both road workers and drivers by clearly marking where it is and is not safe to drive.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the driver in front of you.,b:Relax and concentrate on driving.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: Staying calm, allowing extra travel time, and focusing on safe driving choices helps prevent aggressive driving. Avoid tailgating, speeding, or reacting emotionally to other drivers’ mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: For a left turn from a two‑way street, you should start from the lane nearest the centerline, staying to the right of the centerline. This positions you correctly to turn into the proper lane on the new road.

question: If your tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking sharply.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Brake gently only when the car is under control and you are ready to pull off the road.

question: Where should your hands be positioned when using hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:Left hand between 7 and 8 o'clock and right hand between 4 and 5 o'clock.,b:Left hand between 9 and 10 o'clock and right hand between 2 and 3 o'clock.,c:Left hand between 10 and 11 o'clock and right hand between 1 and 2 o'clock.
note: With hand‑to‑hand (push/pull) steering, place your left hand around 7–8 o’clock and your right hand around 4–5 o’clock. This gives better control, keeps your arms from crossing, and helps you maintain stability if the airbag deploys.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians crossing your path. Only complete the turn when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Use cruise control to hold a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to reduce this risk is to slow down in heavy rain, especially if there is standing water, and make smooth steering and braking inputs.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision, such as when another driver does not see you or is about to move into your lane. Do not use the horn just because someone is in your way or made a mistake if there is no immediate safety risk.

question: Yellow pavement markings separate what?
options: a:Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. A solid yellow line generally means no passing, while a broken yellow line allows passing when it is safe and legal.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting should you use and what should you do with speed?
options: a:Turn on high beams and speed up.,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,c:Increase speed to avoid causing an accident.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility. Slow down so you have more time to react, and if visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary to pedestrians and cross traffic. You do not need to stop unless required for safety.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Try to fight it while driving.,b:Take a break and rest.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should get off the road at a safe place and rest, nap, or switch drivers. Trying to fight sleep or relying on caffeine or other stimulants is unsafe because your reaction time and judgment are already impaired.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic in each lane is moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross the lines when making a permitted left turn or when specifically allowed by signs.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:In order to see potential hazards early.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways, vehicles travel at higher speeds, so situations develop more quickly and you need more time and space to react. Looking farther ahead helps you spot slow traffic, lane closures, and other hazards early so you can adjust smoothly and safely.

question: Why is driving at night generally more dangerous than during the day?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights limit your view, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility, giving you less time to see hazards and react safely.

question: Slowing down to look at collisions or other unusual events along the road tends to:
options: a:Cause traffic congestion.,b:Prevent rear-end collisions.,c:Improve traffic flow.
note: Slowing down just to look at crashes or other events on the road, called rubbernecking, disrupts the normal flow of traffic and often causes congestion and additional collisions. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol concentration can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount of alcohol detected.
note: For drivers under 21, many states, including Kansas, have "zero tolerance" laws. This means that any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while driving can lead to penalties such as license suspension, even if you are below the 0.08% limit that applies to drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:When you can see the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:If you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: After you pass another vehicle, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (usually its headlights) clearly in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of the other vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting them off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: How should you view backing up your vehicle?
options: a:It is safer when a helper is present.,b:It is dangerous only in large vehicles.,c:It is always potentially dangerous and requires caution.
note: Backing up is always potentially dangerous because your view to the rear and sides is limited. You should back slowly, check mirrors and blind spots, and turn your head to look behind you. If possible, use a helper to guide you, especially in tight or crowded areas.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: As daylight fades, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road better. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, or other conditions that reduce visibility, use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road while making your vehicle more visible to others. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and make it harder to see.

question: How should you adjust driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Slow down because tires have less traction than on pavement.,b:Expect better traction than on pavement.,c:Maintain normal highway speeds because visibility is the same.
note: On gravel or dirt, your tires have much less grip than on paved roads. Loose stones and dust increase your stopping distance and make it easier to skid, especially when turning or braking. You should slow down, steer smoothly, and leave extra space so you can stop safely.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop when the bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, except on a divided highway where you are traveling in the opposite direction.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions must stop because children may be crossing the road. The main exception is on a divided highway with a physical median or barrier: in that case, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop. Always be prepared to stop and watch carefully for children near the roadway.

question: What is the only proven way to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Give your body time.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Breathe in fresh air.
note: Nothing speeds elimination of alcohol from the body; only the passage of time lowers BAC and reduces impairment.

question: A broken yellow centerline means which of the following?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may pass another vehicle on the left if the lane is clear and you can complete the pass safely before oncoming traffic or a no‑passing zone.

question: When roads are slippery after the first rain, what driving behavior is recommended?
options: a:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.,b:Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: When it first starts to rain, oil and debris on the road mix with water and make the surface very slippery. You should slow down, increase following distance, and avoid sudden turns or hard braking so your tires can maintain traction and you are less likely to skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge.
note: When pulling away from a curb, you must wait for a gap that allows you to signal, check mirrors and blind spots, then accelerate smoothly to match the speed of traffic without forcing others to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do at an intersection when the traffic control signal is not operating?
options: a:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,b:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: If a traffic signal is dark or not working, treat the intersection like a four‑way stop: come to a complete stop, then proceed in turn, yielding to vehicles that arrived first and to pedestrians and cross traffic as required.

question: What best defines distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that makes you pay extra attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, including taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off the driving task, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rain?
options: a:If it has been raining for several hours.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: When rain first begins, oils and residue on the road mix with the water and create a slick film, making the pavement especially slippery until the buildup is washed away by continued rain.

question: While in a motor vehicle on a highway, what is the rule about open containers of alcohol?
options: a:It is legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.,b:It is illegal in most states to drink from or possess open containers of alcohol in a moving vehicle.,c:It is legal to drink if you are driving but not intoxicated.
note: It is illegal for drivers or passengers to possess open containers of alcohol in a motor vehicle while it is in operation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.
